editorial_angle: Every outlet reported that GTA VI has hurricanes. None could say whether they do anything, because Rockstar has not said: Eurogamer asked outright whether wet roads will affect tyres. This short sits in that gap on purpose. It states the three things that are on record, says plainly what is missing, then switches to a clearly labelled what-if and plays one police chase through a storm to show why the answer matters: if weather is systemic rather than cosmetic, it changes the most repeated moment in the series.
visual_premise: An ordinary high-speed police chase under a clear sky: the escape every player already knows how to run.
visual_escalation: The same chase, the same red car, as a storm arrives. Rain eats the visibility, the street floods, the car slides and a pursuer spins out, the helicopter above cannot hold steady, and the usual way out is under water.
visual_payoff: The driver stops at the flooded underpass he always uses and has to pick a route he has never taken. The weather, not the police, ended the plan.
visual_style: photoreal cinematic car chase, one continuous weather progression from clear sky to hurricane, same hero car throughout
hooks: GTA six's hurricanes could completely change police chases.
What if a hurricane hit in the middle of a GTA six police chase?
Rockstar put hurricanes in GTA six. It hasn't said what they do to a getaway.

voiceover.text: GTA six's hurricanes could completely change police chases.
On record: Rockstar's lighting chief told Game Informer the weather system was re-engineered to be localized and persistent.
He describes heavy clouds, strong winds and a lot of rain, with everything dripping wet.
What Rockstar hasn't said is whether any of it affects how you play. Eurogamer asked the obvious question: will wet roads affect your tyres?
So from here, this is our what-if.
If storms are systemic, rain cuts how far you can see, and streets start to flood.
A helicopter might not hold steady in that wind.
And the escape route you always use is under water.
If Rockstar goes that far, weather isn't decoration. It's the chase. Systemic, or just pretty?

editing_notes: Two visual languages, never mixed. Shots 1-4 carry a green ON RECORD or amber NOT SAID tag; from shot 5 a red WHAT IF badge stays in the top corner until the end card, so a frame grabbed from anywhere in the second half still says it is speculation. Keep the small 'AI-generated visualisation, not game footage' label on screen for the full runtime. The weather only ever gets worse: do not cut back to a dry shot after shot 3. Shots 1 and 6 use the same camera angle on purpose, so the viewer reads it as the same chase before and after; match-cut them through the cards if the timing allows. Shot 5 is two seconds and a hard cut: it is the hinge of the video, give it a beat of near silence. Shots 7, 8 and 9 are fast, one consequence each, cut on the voiceover's full stops. Burned-in captions, two lines maximum. Quote marks on screen only around Shepherd's and Eurogamer's exact words. No game art, no trailer frames, no HUD elements, no wanted stars, no logos: nothing that imitates the game's interface.
sound_music: Open on engine and sirens under a bright, driving bed (licensed library track, no vocals). Duck everything under the ON RECORD card. Distant thunder on shot 3. On the WHAT IF stamp, cut the music dead for half a second, then bring the bed back darker and slower with heavy rain over it. Wind and rotor wash on shot 8, with the rotor pitch wobbling. On shot 9, strip back to rain, an idling engine and one distant siren. End on rain only. Voice: conversational and measured, a clear change of tone at 'our what-if'; never an announcer read.
cta: One question to argue about: systemic, or just pretty? Sources in the description.

youtube_description:
What's on record: Rockstar's Owen Shepherd told Game Informer that GTA VI's weather system was re-engineered to be "much more localized and persistent", with hurricanes, strong winds and heavy rain (reported by Eurogamer and Rock Paper Shotgun).

What isn't: Rockstar has not said whether weather affects driving, police or anything else you do. Eurogamer asked whether wet roads will affect tyres, and there is no answer yet.

Everything after the WHAT IF stamp is our speculation about what a storm could do to a police chase if the weather is systemic. It is not reported and not announced.

AI-generated visualisation. Not actual GTA VI gameplay.
